title: Turon: Crisp Caramel-Glazed Banana and Jackfruit Rolls
summary: Sugared banana and jackfruit wrapped in spring roll pastry, fried until crisp and turned in brown sugar caramel.

ingredients.item: spring roll wrappers, about 20 cm square
ripe saba bananas, halved lengthwise (or 2 ripe plantains, quartered)
ripe jackfruit, fresh or from a jar, drained and cut in thin strips
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Coat the bananas
steps.text: Spread the 100 g brown sugar in the shallow dish and roll each banana piece in it until coated. The sugar melts as they fry and sweetens from within.

steps.title: Roll them up
steps.text: Lay a wrapper as a diamond, set a banana piece across the middle and top with a few jackfruit strips. Fold up the bottom point, fold in the sides and roll firmly, sealing the last point with a dab of water. Fry within 1 h so the wrappers stay crisp rather than soggy.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat about 1 cm of oil in the large pan to 175 °C. Fry the rolls in two batches for 3-4 min, turning, until golden and crisp all over, then drain on the rack.

steps.title: Make the caramel
steps.text: In the second pan, melt the 80 g brown sugar with the 2 tbsp water over medium heat. Let it bubble for 2-3 min until a shade darker and thick enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Add the fried rolls and turn them quickly in the caramel for about 1 min until shiny all over. Work fast, because the caramel keeps darkening.

steps.title: Let it set
steps.text: Return them to the rack for 3 min so the caramel hardens into a crackly shell, then serve warm.

tips: Roll tightly with no air pockets; a common mistake is loose rolls that soak up oil and split.
If you cannot find saba, use firm ripe plantains rather than soft dessert bananas.
Keep the caramel moving and take it off the heat if it darkens too fast.
Seal the wrapper edges well so the sugar does not leak and burn.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten within a few hours. Keep leftovers uncovered at room temperature for up to 1 day; reheat in a 200 °C (180 °C fan) oven for 5-6 min to crisp.
